caveats: The $60 billion figure is a private, primary-share valuation set in the October 2026 funding round; private valuations are mark-based and can move sharply between rounds (it was $44 billion only four months earlier, and roughly $13 billion as recently as July 2025).
No exchange-traded or public market value exists — Ramp remains a private company, so the only current valuation is the round price set October 15, 2026.

passages.quote:
Ramp has surged to $2 billion in annualized revenue, the fintech company plans to announce Thursday — a milestone that’s helped attract fresh investor capital.

The corporate spending management startup has raised $1.85 billion in a new funding round that values it at $60 billion, Ramp confirmed. Dragoneer Investment Group led the round, with Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Sands Capital and Avenir joining as co-leads.

Expense management company Ramp said on Thursday that it had raised $1.85 billion in a new funding round that values it at $60 billion, just four months after raising $750 million at a [$44 billion valuation](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/04/ramp-raises-750m-at-44b-valuation-as-investors-hunger-for-fintechs-with-an-ai-story/).

Ramp said its annualized revenue has crossed $2 billion, up from a [reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-06-04/ramp-notches-44-billion-valuation-in-new-funding-round) $1.5 billion in June, and that its revenue growth is 25% faster than it was around this time last year. The company claims it now facilitates annualized purchase volume of over $275 billion, up 175% from a year earlier. It also says it has 85,000 customers, up from 70,000 in June, including Visa, Uber, Shopify, Robinhood, Anduril, Notion, Cursor, and Figma.
